name: Czech Republic
summary: Czechia exempts gains on securities held more than 3 years, and from 2026 without any annual cap, has no inheritance tax and exempts gifts from relatives, and has no wealth tax. Dividends cost a flat 15%. For a long-term buy-and-hold investor it is one of the most favourable regimes in the EU.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Progressive PIT 15%/23% with time-test exemptions for capital gains.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident with a permanent home in Czechia or 183+ days of presence in a calendar year.

capital_gains.summary: There is no separate capital gains tax: gains are ordinary income taxed at 15%, or 23% above CZK 1,762,812 (2026). But gains on listed shares and bonds held more than 3 years are fully exempt (time test), as are gains on a stake in a limited company (s.r.o.) held more than 5 years and on real estate held more than 10 years (5 years if bought before 2021). From 2026 there is no cap on the securities exemption: the CZK 40m annual cap that applied in 2025 now applies only to crypto-assets (§4(3)), confirmed in the consolidated law text.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Time test: 3 years for securities (shares, bonds, fund units); 5 years for company stakes not represented by a security; real estate 10 years (acquired from 2021) or 5 years (earlier), 2 years for a main residence lived in. Small sales: total gross proceeds from securities up to CZK 100,000 a year are exempt regardless of holding period.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: The exemption does not apply to securities held as business assets, or sold within 3 years of being withdrawn from business assets.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: 2025 only: exempt income from securities and stakes was capped at CZK 40 million per year; the excess was taxable. From 1 January 2026 the cap in §4(3) applies only to crypto-assets (§4(1)(zk)); securities and company stakes are uncapped (law text version 157, effective 1 Aug 2026, checked 15 Oct 2026). Exempt income above CZK 5 million must be reported to the tax office by the return deadline (§38v ZDP, confirmed in the law text); failure to report carries a penalty.

sources.title: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb., o daních z příjmů (consolidated, version effective 1.8.2026)
Czech Republic - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: The brief mentioned a CZK 100m annual cap introduced in 2025: not found. The law in force (version effective 1 Aug - 31 Dec 2026) shows the CZK 40m cap now only in §4(3) for crypto-assets; securities and company stakes are uncapped from 2026.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Assumes holdings longer than the time tests (3 years securities, 5 years s.r.o. stake, 10 years real estate): exempt, 0. Short-term gains: 23% marginal for a large gain (15% up to CZK 1,762,812). No social or health insurance on these 'other income' gains.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities held in business assets or trading as a business fall outside the time test and are taxed as business income (with social and health insurance).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 3 years for securities, 5 years for unlisted company stakes, 10 years for real estate (from 2021 acquisitions), 2 years main residence.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Time test applies to foreign securities and foreign real estate alike; worldwide taxation for residents.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Czech companies are taxed by a final 15% withholding tax. Foreign dividends can be put into a separate tax base taxed at a flat 15% (or into the general base at 15%/23%), with credit for foreign withholding tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: No allowance against the separate 15% base.

Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb., o daních z příjmů (consolidated, version effective 1.8.2026)

dividends.rate_basis: Czech dividends: 15% final WHT. Foreign dividends: flat 15% separate base (§16a), foreign WHT credited up to the treaty rate.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% on dividends to residents of EU/EEA and treaty/information-exchange countries, 35% to others; reduced by treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
dividends.treaty_network: Wide network covering the EU, the US and most OECD states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: A Czech company pays 21% CIT; dividends from qualifying subsidiaries are exempt under the participation exemption; distribution to an individual then bears 15%. No holding structure is scored for Czechia: listed securities held personally for more than 3 years are tax-exempt (uncapped from 2026), whereas a Czech company pays 21% on portfolio gains and a 15% special rate on portfolio dividends (the participation exemption needs at least 10% held 12 months) and distributions bear another 15%, so a holding company is worse on every line.

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual real estate tax on property owned at 1 January, based on area, type, use and municipal coefficients; small for residential property. No real estate transfer tax.

inheritance.summary: There is no inheritance tax: inherited assets are exempt from income tax for every heir. There is no separate gift tax either: gifts are income of the recipient, but gifts from relatives in the direct line (children, grandchildren) and the collateral line (siblings and others) and from spouses are exempt.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Inheritance (§4a(a)): fully exempt for any heir. Gifts from relatives (§10(3)(c)(1)): exempt without limit. Exempt gifts/inheritances above CZK 5 million must be reported to the tax office (§38v ZDP, confirmed in the law text).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Gifts received from non-relatives are taxable income (15%/23%) subject to small exemptions. Exempt income above CZK 5m may need to be reported (unverified).

sources.title: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb., o daních z příjmů (consolidated, version effective 1.8.2026)

open_questions: Notary probate fees not quantified; treated as negligible.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; gifts are income but gifts from relatives (direct and collateral line) are exempt.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Exemption applies regardless of where the assets are.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Income tax residence (permanent home or 183 days).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a permanent home (owned or rented, intended for permanent living) in Czechia or is present 183+ days in a calendar year (arrival and departure days count). Treaty tie-breakers resolve dual residence.

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.requirements: Register residence for stays over 3 months; no investment requirement.

routes.name: Long-term visa / residence permit
routes.requirements: Permit for a purpose such as business, employment or family; Czechia has no investor visa programme as far as found (unverified).

corporate.summary: 21% CIT for tax periods from 2024 (19% before). Participation exemption for dividends and share gains from qualifying subsidiaries.

sources.title: Czech Republic - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

us_citizen_notes: A US-Czech income tax treaty is in force. The Czech time-test exemption does not shelter gains from US tax.
open_questions: Any income tax changes announced by the government formed after the October 2025 election were not found in PwC (reviewed July 2026) or in the law version effective 1 Aug 2026.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 48 distinct houses/villas of 200-400 m² for rent in Prague's prime western and southern districts (Praha 6: Dejvice, Bubeneč, Střešovice, Nebušice, Vokovice, Veleslavín, Suchdol; Praha 5; Praha 4/Podolí/Braník), sampled from Sreality.cz on 15 Oct 2026 (range CZK 49,999-190,000; median of all 67 Prague listings in that size band CZK 85,000). Asking rents, utilities extra.

source.title: Pronájem domu od 200 m² do 400 m² Praha (listing search)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: International School of Prague, Grades 11-12, academic year 2026/27: tuition CZK 753,000 plus annual Capital Assessment Fee CZK 78,000. New students also pay a one-off Newcomers' Fee of CZK 52,000 and a CZK 9,000 application fee.
